segments.text: a five-year-old girl is weighed at the post office, stamped, and mailed.
Her parents just did. {53|Fifty-three} cents in stamps, on her coat: cheaper than a train ticket.
She weighs forty-eight and a half pounds. The parcel limit is fifty.
So she rides the mail train, {73|seventy-three} miles across Idaho, in the mail car.
And she isn't the first. A year earlier, in Ohio, a baby boy went by post: {15|fifteen} cents, insured for {$50|fifty dollars}.
Nobody rides in a sack, though. The mail clerk travelling with her is her mother's cousin.
He walks her to her grandmother's door. Delivered.
Then the Post Office bans it: no more humans in the mail.
And the next year, parents post their kids anyway.
